Why Small Agencies Lose Clients in the Second Year

The first year with a new client is usually busy and full of visible wins. The website is rebuilt, the campaigns launch and the reports show steady growth from a low starting point. The trouble often starts in the second year, when the easy improvements are gone and the client begins to ask what the retainer is still paying for.

Agencies that keep clients through this stage tend to change how they report. Instead of listing tasks completed, they tie every piece of work to one or two business numbers the client already tracks, such as qualified leads or repeat orders. They also agree on a short list of experiments for the year ahead, so that progress does not depend on a single channel.
